Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of characterization and tone / mood shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.)
content.exemplar: Mrs. Bennet's behaviour at Netherfield damages the reputation she is trying to promote. When the text says “She performed her part indeed without much graciousness, but Mrs. Bennet was satisfied” (Chapter IX, paragraph 35), it shows this directly. She leaves "satisfied" after a visit in which Elizabeth has had to manage her, showing that she cannot see the impression her family makes; Lydia's demand for a ball adds to it.

hsSenior.note: Weigh competing interpretations; students should defend the stronger reading.
